summary: Anthropic is expanding its Project Glasswing cybersecurity program, giving roughly 150 additional organizations across more than 15 countries and new critical-infrastructure sectors access to its Claude Mythos Preview model to scan codebases for vulnerabilities, while also releasing a Claude Security product and internal tooling to trusted security teams.

mechanisms.reason: A large expansion in the number of organizations running Mythos Preview at scale to scan codebases increases aggregate inference volume for this workload.
mechanisms.quote: we’re extending the partnership to approximately 150 new organizations

practices.reason: Security teams gain a new gated tool and product surface (Claude Security, plus request-based Glasswing tooling) that would need evaluation before integration into a security pipeline.
practices.quote: We're also releasing—on request, to trusted security teams— the tools we developed to help Project Glasswing’s partners find vulnerabilities more quickly.

practices.reason: The described triage and disclosure practices for handling large volumes of AI-surfaced vulnerabilities describe a measurement/verification workflow relevant to teams assessing model-found security issues, though the methodology itself is lab-internal and not handed over as a reusable instrument.
practices.quote: We’re also working on sharing ideas and best practices for disclosing vulnerabilities to open-source maintainers, with the intent of making these reports easier to triage and to act upon.
